issues.title: Abstract universal no-PTAS overclaim

failure_location.quote:
We show that these criteria 
are NP hard and do not admit polynomial time approximation schemes (PTAS).

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
In the case $p=2$, minimizing the Frobenius norm 
can be accomplished by a polynomial time algorithm

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract claims that every criterion in the preceding list does not admit a PTAS. The old paper actually states that direct Frobenius-norm minimization has an exact polynomial-time algorithm, and its summary table does not claim no-PTAS results for every listed Schatten-norm criterion. An exact polynomial-time algorithm supplies a PTAS, so the universal abstract claim both contradicts one listed case and exceeds the established inapproximability results.
issues.overall_effect: The abstract overstates the scope of the paper's PTAS-inapproximability results; the individual body theorems are unaffected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Make an abstract-only scope correction by replacing the universal no-PTAS conjunct with a qualified statement such as “many of these criteria do not admit polynomial-time approximation schemes (PTAS),” or by restricting it explicitly to the criteria for which no-PTAS results are established. No body theorem or proof needs alteration.
issues.why_classification: The old introduction and summary table already limit the no-PTAS results, while direct Frobenius-norm minimization has an exact polynomial-time algorithm. The universal abstract statement is therefore a coherent but substantive inapproximability overclaim, not a transcriptional typo. Repair necessarily retracts universal scope, so it is more than a same-guarantee minor edit; nevertheless, the supported claim that many criteria admit no PTAS is recognizably comparable, and the correction is wholly local with no affected formal results or proof reconstruction. The resulting loss is limited rather than major.

new_version_repair_locator.quote:
We show that these criteria 
are NP hard and \changes{many} do not admit polynomial time approximation schemes (PTAS).
